culture.hero_subtitle: Vodoun, Gèlèdè, food, crafts, music: discover the traditions at the heart of Benin.
culture.intro_text: In Benin, culture is not kept behind glass: it lives in ceremonies, markets, workshops and festivals. These pages help you understand what you will see, and visit with respect.
culture.events_text: Highlights to meet Beninese culture. Dates vary: ask us before booking.

categories.title: Vodoun
categories.subtitle: A religion born in Benin
categories.longDescription: Vodoun is a religion practised for centuries along the Gulf of Benin. It honours deities linked to nature and ancestors. Ouidah is one of its major centres, and 10 January is a national holiday. Ceremonies are sacred: attend only with the initiates' consent.

categories.title: Gèlèdè
categories.subtitle: Masks in honour of mothers
categories.longDescription: Gèlèdè is a mask tradition of the Yoruba/Nagô people in south-eastern Benin. Dances, songs and costumes honour the power of women and mothers. UNESCO has listed it as intangible cultural heritage of humanity.

categories.title: Cuisine
categories.subtitle: Flavours on every street corner
categories.longDescription: Beninese cuisine combines grains, tubers, fish, spicy sauces and palm oil. Maize paste, pounded yam, rice, grilled fish and fritters are found in restaurants and markets alike.

categories.title: Crafts
categories.subtitle: Hands that create
categories.longDescription: Basketry, pottery, weaving, wood carving and bronze casting: Beninese crafts are passed down through generations. Visiting a workshop means buying directly from the makers.

categories.title: Music and dance
categories.subtitle: The rhythm of ceremonies
categories.longDescription: Drums, songs and dances set the pace of ceremonies, weddings and festivals. Each region has its own instruments and rhythms, from south to north.

categories.title: Festivals
categories.subtitle: A calendar full of life
categories.longDescription: Traditional feasts, festivals and celebrations mark the year. Dates follow the local calendar: ask us before planning your trip.
